title: Legends of Jazz recordings 1973-78
summary: Redd lists the Minneapolis and Hollywood Legends of Jazz sessions with personnel and tunes, including Blakeney's vocals.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: 1973, Crescent Productions presents the Legends of Jazz on the Legends of Jazz label, recorded in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The personnel included Andy Blakeney; Joe Darensbourg; Louis Nelson; Alton Purnell; Ed Montudie Garland; Barry Martyn, Drums.

The songs performed on this date were 'Conti Street Parade'; 'Out in the Cold Again'; 'The Legends Boogie'; 'Apex Blues'; 'Down Among the Sheltering Palms'; 'Louisiana IA'; 'Just a Little While to Stay Here'; 'Old Man Mose'; 'The Redman Blues'; and 'Do You Know What it Means to Miss New Orleans.'
On the latter Mr. Blakeney does a vocal. This was recorded in Minneapolis, Minnesota, 1973, Legends of Jazz label, Legends of Jazz group.
1974, May 29 and 30 of 1974; Hollywood, California, the Legends of Jazz are presented by the Crescent Jazz Productions. The personnel on this date along
with Mr. Blakeney included Barney Bigard; Joe Darensbourg; Louis Nelson; Alton Purnell; Montudie--that is Ed Garland; Barry Martyn.

On these series of recordings Andy Blakeney also does a vocal which is on 'Back of Town Blues.' The numbers performed were, 'Legends Funky Blues,' which featured Barney Bigard; 'I Surrender Dear,' Alton Purnell the vocalist as well as pianist; 'Black and White Rag,' 'Yellow Dog Blues,' 'Creole Love Call,' 'High Society' and 'Where or When.' This was done in Hollywood, California May 29 and 30, 1974, Crescent Jazz Productions presents the Legends of Jazz.
